summary: AV transitive build, head8/B128 teacher mapping, new training-only bank binding, GT-camera evaluation, native/full50 and paired state/order gates pass source inspection and labelled stdlib mocked flow checks. One measured disk-admission defect blocks launching this R1 private launcher.

blocking_findings.title: 2.1 GB admission is below the measured retained output footprint of the unchanged AV pair
blocking_findings.finding: The generated remote launcher accepts free space greater than 2,100,000,000 bytes. The historical same-architecture AV pair retained six required best/raw/state binaries totaling 2,087,690,537 bytes. Its two still-present, manifest/SHA-verified batch_orders.jsonl files add 120,716,915 bytes. That lower bound is 2,208,407,452 bytes, exceeding admission by 108,407,452 bytes before the other manifests, epoch/per-query outputs, reference outputs, or source package. All 273 archived remote text files were independently verified now and total 148,861,503 bytes; binaries plus those text outputs total 2,236,552,040 bytes. The new controller retains both controls through state evaluation and has no intervening offload, so the admitted range includes a measured insufficient-capacity case.
blocking_findings.consequence: A job can pass admission, spend both full50 training budgets, and fail while writing required arrays/states. The review does not claim that current remote free space is insufficient; no remote query was made.
blocking_findings.minimal_fix: Raise only the existing free-space threshold to cover the measured pair footprint and its extra reference/staging outputs; the parent-proposed 3,000,000,000-byte threshold provides 763,447,960 bytes above the measured prior binaries-plus-text total. Preserve this R1 and submit the changed private launcher for bounded re-review. No fallback, cleanup or model change is needed.
